channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Harris County settles $1.25 million federal lawsuit from special needs teen’s beating death inside jail
item.description: The civil rights lawsuit emerged in 2022, nearly a year after 19-year-old, 98-pound Fred Harris was attacked and beaten to death inside a jail cell by an inmate nearly twice his size.

item.title: Plans unveiled for ‘Toro District,’ the Houston Texans’ forthcoming headquarters in northwest Harris County
item.description: The total cost of the mixed-use development, expected to be completed in 2029, has not been revealed. Local taxpayers will foot the bill for the county’s infrastructure, including a community services hub within the 83-acre complex.

item.title: Texas declared independence 190 years ago. This town northwest of Houston is celebrating
item.description: Almost two centuries ago, dozens of Texans gathered in the town of Washington-on-the-Brazos to sign Texas’ Declaration of Independence from Mexico. Today, the site is investing in becoming a historical destination.

item.title: Exclusive: $70 million annual goal for Houston’s homeless fund will be ‘reevaluated’ after shortfall
item.description: The city fell short by nearly $40 million, and it's unclear if the fundraising sources it secured last year will be renewed. The shortfall marked a blow to Mayor John Whitmire's effort to "end street homelessness" in Houston.

item.title: Hello Houston (February 26, 2026)
item.description: Today: We hear the latest episode of Brandon Rottinghaus’ Texperts, talk with actor and comedian Mae Martin, and learn about the Bryan Museum’s large collection of historical artifacts.

item.title: Prayer in Texas schools (Feb. 26, 2026)
item.description: On Thursday's show: The deadline is next week for Texas public school boards to vote on whether or not to adopt a voluntary period for prayer and reading of religious texts during the school day. We discuss SB 11 and concerns over how it will be implemented.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 26, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Lawsuit says charges against Houston man were dropped before fatal struggle with officers in jail
item.description: A kiosk for inmates to charge their cell phones upon their release from the jail is located in the re-entry services area of the jail, which closes at 5 p.m. during weekdays.

item.title: Harris County commissioners condemn ICE operations, call on federal government to enact reforms
item.description: Commissioners voted 3-1 to pass a resolution directing local law enforcement agencies to stick to clear and consistent processes while detaining and relocating individuals regardless of their immigration status.

item.title: Houston ISD board votes to close 12 schools, angering audience at meeting
item.description: The state-appointed board of managers voted unanimously Thursday on the closures, which will take effect after this school year. The decision came two weeks after Superintendent Mike Miles surprised the community with the recommendation, leading to fierce criticism about a lack of public engagement.
